response: Mental imagery functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) can predict recovery in patients with disorders of consciousness, particularly those in a vegetative state (VS). The fMRI paradigm mental imagery has shown a high concordance with the further clinical course of patients in a VS. Patients in a VS who showed significant activation of regions of interest (ROIs) had a favorable further course, and may benefit from rehabilitation treatment. However, in cases where no significant activation was seen, the method has no prognostic value. Additionally, the prediction of the clinical course of patients in a minimally conscious state (MCS) by fMRI was less accurate than in patients in a VS. These patients may be referred to as being in a "functional minimally conscious state" and may benefit from rehabilitation treatment.
